question.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14268503/assets/ae5c0c967a0ddd28c163a51aca44edc3340cb76a2f9da28704563b423c591de8.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14268503/assets/9afd33bf9d62d13ceab462ed9705c007173253b065b347c6475acbff5b8090fe.svg) be vectors such that $\mathbf{u} \!\perp\! \mathbf{w}$. Find $(\mathbf{u}+\mathbf{v})\cdot \mathbf{w} + \mathbf{u}\cdot(\mathbf{v}+ \mathbf{w}).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{w}$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}=0$. Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u+v)\cdot w+u\cdot (v+w) & =u\cdot w+v\cdot w+u\cdot v+u\cdot w \\  & =0+v\cdot w+u\cdot v+0 \\  & =v\cdot w+u\cdot v \\  & =(2\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 3+4\cdot 1) \\  & +((-1)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-3)+5\cdot 4)\, \\  & =(-2-9+4)+(-2+6+20) \\  & =-7+24 \\  & =17.\end{aligned}
$$
